title: A Solar Storm Blacked Out Quebec in 90 Seconds

scenes.text: A storm from the Sun shut down a whole power grid in ninety seconds.
It happened on March thirteenth, 1989, just before three in the morning.
A huge burst of charged particles from the Sun hit Earth's magnetic field.
That sent strong currents through the ground and into power lines.
A transformer failed, and Quebec's whole grid collapsed.
Six million people lost power for about nine hours. One storm from the Sun, ninety seconds.

description:
A storm from the Sun shut down a whole power grid in ninety seconds.
On March 13, 1989, a geomagnetic storm collapsed Quebec's grid and left about six million people without power for roughly nine hours.
Could you handle nine hours without power?
first_comment: One solar storm, six million people in the dark. What would you do for nine hours?
